newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa pares 3.7 pct in spec selling.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa pares 3.7 pct in spec selling.

text.p: Cocoa futures seemed to have derailed from their recent upward track after a 3.7 percent loss on Monday that took the market to a four-month floor.

Speculators relentlessly unloaded their long positions after the market triggered key chart levels. While traders see the prospects of the market bottoming out at these levels, they were sceptical of an immediate rebound.
"It's difficult to see why the market should go significantly higher," said one trader. "But I think it's bottoming out."
Another trader said: "Cocoa has done its bit now but I'm not surprised if more selling emerges."
All-day long fund and spec liquidation sent benchmark September to a four-month low of 977 stg per tonne at one stage. It still ended sharply lower at 985 stg for a 30 stg loss on the day.
It had broken the psychologically-important 1,000 stg support in the first 25 minutes of trading, and then tested the 988 stg low after filling a chart gap at 989-1,010 left since March 11.
Traders said trade buying on the dips helped slow the decline in the afternoon.
September absorbed most of 16,968 lots with a volume of 7,989.
Cocoa's sell-off also run into active producer selling, some traders said.
Monday's setback put the market back to way it started in March when it emerged from the gloom and boom of a nine-month downtrend.
Funds were said to be behind the buying in March. But since then, they had liquidated their long positions and probably had gone short now.
On the charts, September will find a strong support at 950. Resistance is seen at 1,000.
Cocoa's technical picture looked more promising until the major setback on July 3 when prices lost more than 100 stg on one day alone.
The market had peaked at 1,170 two days earlier before the speculative sell-off set in.
On the fundamental front, even the rosy second-quarter U.S. grind data released on Friday and coming after a lacklustre European figures failed to encourage the buyers.
Elsewhere, crop analysts and regional buyers said Ivorian 1997/98 crop was developing strongly with large harvests possible if favourable weather continues into August.

The U.S. CFTC Commitment of Traders released late on Friday showed that while the fund long positions had been reduced by around 6,000 lots, the funds remained very long of New York cocoa, broker GNI said.
